sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Yogendra Pal Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. appearing for the State.
It has been contended by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case on the basis of suspicion.
The applicant has not committed the alleged offence.
There is no eye witness of the alleged incident.

It is next contended that the co-accused Sumit Kumar has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 10.04.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.15209 of 2023, therefore, the applicant is also entitled for bail on the ground of parity.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.15209 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed forth before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused has also been touched upon at length.

It has been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and Radha Devi vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191215623/
1 shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has also been submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 28.02.2023.
It has been pointed out that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

Considering the nature of accusation and the severity of punishment in case of conviction and the nature of supporting evidence, reasonable apprehension of tempering of the witnesses, enlargement of co-accused on bail and prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge and reformative theory of punishment the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.

Let the applicant Radha Devi, involved in Case Crime No.95 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468,
471, 120-B I.P.C. & 66 I.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali Fatehgarh, District Farrukhabad be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she will not tamper with the evidence and will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses and will cooperate with the trial.
The applicant shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 22.5.2023 Jitendra  Radha Devi vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191215623/
